source.title: Hi-ZFO: Hierarchical Zeroth- and First-Order LLM Fine-Tuning via Importance-Guided Tensor Selection

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the paper through its appendices; no cutoff or garbling that prevents extraction is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports fine-tuning performance, optimizer comparisons, and ablations on generative tasks. These results do not measure train-versus-test error, random-label memorization, the mapped architecture/batch-size/regularization conditions, or a trained-network property tracking that gap. Its relevant claims concern fine-tuning performance and generalization more broadly, which do not test the specified versions.
record.gate_note: The tables compare downstream benchmark scores and training costs for fine-tuning methods; the paper does not report training error versus held-out error or the behaviors measured by V1–V8. The optimizer and ZO-loss ablations concern a hybrid LLM fine-tuning method, not V4's adaptive-optimizer comparison or V6's dropout intervention.
record.test_reason: The study compares hybrid first-/zeroth-order LLM fine-tuning with other fine-tuning methods. None of its results tests V1–V8: it provides no random-label experiment, width-to-interpolation sweep, convolutional comparison, adaptive-versus-SGD comparison, controlled batch-size intervention, dropout intervention, sharpness–gap correlation, or memorized-example removal experiment.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' conclusion: they attribute improved downstream performance and reduced training time and memory to combining first-order precision with zeroth-order exploration. Their claim of consistent superiority is broader than the tables support: full fine-tuning wins on Math500 and OPT-350M WebQuestions. Escape from sharp minima and reduced overfitting are proposed explanations, not directly established by sharpness or generalization-gap measurements.
record.recipe_differences: Hybrid first- and zeroth-order fine-tuning of pretrained LLMs on generative, mathematical, and coding benchmarks; not the methods or measurements specified in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports performance changes with the FLOPs-based update ratio, ZO learning-rate ratio, and ZO-loss weight; these are ablations of Hi-ZFO rather than conditions mapped by the claim versions.

fits_no_version.finding: On Qwen2-7B, Hi-ZFO exceeds full fine-tuning on GSM8K (0.810 versus 0.773) and HumanEval (0.564 versus 0.505), but trails it on Math500 (0.350 versus 0.370; Table 2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Hybrid first-/zeroth-order supervised fine-tuning can improve downstream LLM performance relative to full fine-tuning, with task-dependent gains.

fits_no_version.finding: Removing the perturbed-loss contribution lowers OPT-2.7B DialogSum ROUGE-1 from 26.7 to 23.1 (Table 5). This intervention changes the hybrid objective rather than dropout or an adaptive-versus-SGD comparison.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Including a weighted perturbed loss can improve downstream performance within Hi-ZFO.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (as stated in the supplied metadata)
record.problems: The study's results do not measure train/test generalization gaps. The reported benchmark scores and fine-tuning ablations therefore cannot establish the claim versions' outcomes.
record.rows_left_out: No rows: none of the reported outcomes measures the claim's specified behaviors.

untested.parts: Coexistence of random-label fitting and natural-label generalization, including chance-level held-out performance with random labels.
Test-error changes when width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classifier generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning, including switching optimizers and decoupled weight decay.
Large- versus small-batch held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Effects of dropout, training-set size, and joint dropout/weight-decay removal with augmentation.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance ranking generalization gaps, including comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Change the record's relation from tests to discusses; retain T6 and no version-specific verdicts. The empty row set is appropriate for V1–V8. Held-out scores can test several versions without a train/test-gap measurement; exclusion here rests on the missing version-specific comparisons. Perturbations used during optimization do not themselves measure V7's magnitude-aware sharpness–gap relationship.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural labels are not measured.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold test.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparison under the stated tuning conditions.
No large-batch comparison under fixed epoch budgets.
No dropout intervention or dropout/weight-decay removal comparison.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or generalization-gap measurement.
No memorized-example removal and retraining comparison.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
